title: Storage Accounting and Performance
objective: Make storage numbers trustworthy and the scanner inexpensive enough for continuous use.

stories.title: Reclaimability estimator
stories.outcome: Distinguish logical size, allocated size, shared/clone uncertainty, and expected reclaim on supported filesystems.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown APFS/reflink/shared-block effects are never presented as guaranteed savings.
verification: Filesystem-specific integration tests and conservative fallback tests.

stories.title: Performance guardrails
acceptance_criteria: Fast CI benchmarks catch large regressions.
Scheduled deep benchmarks publish trends without blocking ordinary PRs on noisy metrics.
verification: Benchmark workflow and regression-threshold unit tests.

stories.title: Verifier repair: reclaim probe authority and risk correction
stories.outcome: Independent review found E10-S01's CR2 declaration below the CR4 floor because its released batch added unsafe macOS statfs FFI to cancellai-sealedfs. Record the independent CR4 classification without rewriting shipped E10-S01, place the FFI authority in an ADR, and preserve the probe's conservative read-only behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: The independent CR4 classification of released E10-S01 is visible in the risk-classification control plane.
An accepted ADR authorizes the narrowly scoped statfs FFI in cancellai-sealedfs and names its safety and compatibility limits.
If a probe path contains an interior NUL, is missing, or yields a non-UTF-8 type name, then the system shall reject or downgrade the observation without granting mutation authority.
verification: Native macOS sealedfs and platform tests exercise real and missing paths; Miri is attempted and any unavailable component is recorded.
The CR4 Safety Verdict names the FFI boundary, test evidence, residual platform limits, and owner-authorized acceptance.
